newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: China protests Taiwan's presence at tourism talks.
newsitem.headline: China protests Taiwan's presence at tourism talks.

text.p: China protested on Tuesday against the Philippines' decision to invite Taiwan to the World Tourism Organisation meeting in Manila, saying it violated the one-China policy.

Chinese ambassador Guan Ding-ming verbally relayed Beijing's displeasure at Manila's action during a call on Asia-Pacific desk chief Lauro Baja of the Department of Foreign Affairs, a senior Filipino official said.
"They want the non-participation of Taiwan at the meeting," said the official, asking not to be named. "They said it is a violation of our one-China policy."
About 60 countries are taking part in the two-day meeting opening on Thursday. The meeting will discuss the impact on tourism of social problems such as drug addiction, prostitution and child abuse.
China's three-member delegation was already in Manila while Taiwan's two-member team was scheduled to arrive on Wednesday.

Taiwan was invited to the conference by the Philippine tourism department without the knowledge of the foreign affairs department, which learned of the invitation only last weekend, the official said.
The official did not say what action the government would take over the Chinese protest but said Manila's one-China policy "refers only to political and economic matters."
Beijing considers Taiwan a renegade province and insists it is the sole legitimate government of all of China.
